subject: Timeseries scatterplot transforming binary data into counts for the year

messages.author: 7afc9426da77a5e3
messages.subject: Timeseries scatterplot transforming binary data into counts for the year
parts:
I have a dataset that has multiple observations/year and I want to plot a variable but it is binary. Obviously just plotting this does me nothing. Instead, I would like to get a count of the number of times the value is true or false (in each year) and plot that number per year. 

If someone could show how to do this using this code that'd be fantastic 

df <- data.frame(x=c("1991", "1991","1991", "1992", "1992","1992", "1993","1993","1993"), y=c("0", "1","1","0","0","1","0","1","1"))


Thanks,

Darin

messages.subject: Re: Timeseries scatterplot transforming binary data into counts for the year
parts:
Or all in a single line, simpler and better:

qplot(x,y,data=df1,stat="summary",fun.y="sum",geom="bar")

On Fri, Sep 6, 2013 at 2:26 PM, Ben Bond-Lamberty <bpb...@gmail.com> wrote:
> A simple example:
>
> df$y <- as.numeric(df$y)
> df1 <- aggregate(y~x,data=df,FUN=sum)
> ggplot(df1,aes(x,y))+geom_bar(stat="identity")
>
> Ben

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: Timeseries scatterplot transforming binary data into counts for the year
parts:
I'm sure there's a slick one-liner to do this, but this works:

library(plyr)
df1 <- ddply(df,.(x,y),.fun='nrow')
qplot(x,nrow,data=df1,fill=y,geom='bar',stat="identity")

Ben
